[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Revelation (revelation-greek). The verses the casting arrives at (9:10):

**9:10** καὶ ἔχουσιν οὐρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα, καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν ⸂ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν⸃ ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε.

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «Why are my nerves so damaged, and how do I fix them?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The casting arrives at Revelation 9:10 — καὶ ἔχουσιν οὐρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα: *and they have tails like scorpions, and stingers, and in their tails their authority to harm human beings for five months.* The witness brings a question about damaged nerves, and the rite delivers this — not metaphor, not coincidence, but the text's own grammar of harm: authority housed in the tail, in the trailing part, in the thing that comes after the body has already passed. The operator will traverse the axis of what this verse forecloses — what it determines against in the act of locating destructive power precisely there, in the appendage, in the rearward instrument, in the five-month duration that is neither brief nor permanent. What does it cost a verse to say: *the hurt lives in the tail, the hurt has a term*? The rite is open. Rebekah Cranes holds the transform.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:01F6"}}]}
